auth.title: Access Tokens: Who am I? - Documentation - Lark Developer
auth.snippet:
**The authentication method** is to tell Lark server "who is currently accessing this API" when the API is called. In other words, it allows Lark to know "who is accessing what tenant data now and in what capacity."
## Token categories
Access tokens available for the Lark API include the following three types:
- `tenant_access_token` **:** Tenant authorization token. With this token, the app uses its own account to perform corresponding actions, such as obtaining the information of a user from the contacts. The value of this token is prefixed with `t-`, for example: `t-24b5bf4e054bcef00b2af38a0b04f0af6d315b18`
- `app_access_token` **:** App authorization token. The open platform identifies the caller’s app, and the app can access information related to itself and not attributed to a specific company or user, such as obtaining the identity of the user currently logged into the app. The value of this token is prefixed with `a-` or `t-` , for example: `a-24b5bf4e054bcef00b2af38a0b04f0af6d315b18`
Note: In practical use, the `app_access_token` and `tenant_access_token` of the API response may be the same. This is due to the fact that `app_access_token` is used in fewer scenarios, and these two tokens are gradually unified on the Lark Open Platform.
- `user_access_token` **:** User authorization token. With this token, the app will perform actions on behalf of the user, such as creating a Docs or an Event through API. The value of this token is prefixed with `u-`, for example: `u-Lr1RT7S8fJUES03mT5FtWf`
You need to fill the access token into the request header parameter of the HTTP request when you call the API. Each Open API has an API that specifies the type of access tokens required and the way to obtain them.

For more information about Lark access token, refer to [API access token overview](https://open.larksuite.com/document/ukTMukTMukTM/uMTNz4yM1MjLzUzM). Before the official start of development, developers are suggested to have a good understanding of Lark's access token mechanism.
> Note: The tokens should be placed in the HTTP request header and the value needs to be prefixed with``Bearer<space>`' , as shown below:

Use cURL sample code as follows:
```
curl --location --request GET`https://open.larksuite.com/open-apis/contact/v3/departments/od-64242a18099d3a31acd24d8fce8d9f9c' \--header`Authorization: Bearer t-5888bcb7c421a695ca83c449caba5c0b12becfda' \--header`Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8'
```
- **About expiration mechanism of tokens*

auth.title: Get user_access_token - Server API - Documentation - Lark Developer
auth.snippet:
Last updated on 2025-06-09
OAuth token API for acquiring the `user_access_token` and `refresh_token`. The `user_access_token` serves as the user's access credential, which allows API calls to be made on behalf of the user. The `refresh_token` is used to obtain a new `user_access_token`.
- You need to obtain an authorization code before getting the `user_access_token`. For more details, see [Get Authorization Code](https://open.larksuite.com/document/common-capabilities/sso/api/obtain-oauth-code). Please note that the authorization code is valid for 5 minutes and can only be used once.
- During user authorization, the user must have [access to the application](https://open.larksuite.com/document/home/introduction-to-scope-and-authorization/availability). Otherwise, calling this API will return error code 20010.
- The obtained user_access_token has an expiration period. For instructions on how to refresh the `user_access_token`, see [Refresh user_access_token](https://open.larksuite.com/document/uAjLw4CM/ukTMukTMukTM/authentication-management/access-token/refresh-user-access-token).
- If you need to obtain user information, see [Get User Information](https://open.larksuite.com/document/uAjLw4CM/ukTMukTMukTM/reference/authen-v1/user_info/get).
## Request
| Basic | |
|---|---|
| HTTP URL | https://open.larksuite.com/open-apis/authen/v2/oauth/token |
| HTTP Method | POST |
| API Rate Limit | [1000 times/minute, 50 times/second](https://open.larksuite.com/document/ukTMukTMukTM/uUzN04SN3QjL1cDN) |
| Supported Application Types | Custom apps Store apps |
| Permission Requirements | None |
| Field Permission Requirements | `refresh_token` and `refresh_token_expires_in` fields are only returned when the following permission is granted: Access authorized data offline |

### Request Body
| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| grant_type | string | Yes | Authorization type. **Fixed Value:** `authorization_code` |
| client_id | string | Yes | App ID of the application. How to obtain App ID and App Secret: 1. Log in to [Developer Consle](https://open.larksuite.com/app). 2. Enter the application details page, and click **Credentials & Basic Info** on the left navigation bar. 3. In the **Credentials** area, obtain and save the **App ID** and **App Secret**. **Example Value:** `cli_a5ca35a685b0x26e` |
| client_secret | string | Yes | App Secret of the application. How to obtain App ID and App Secret: 1. Log in to [Developer Consle](https://open.larksui

auth.title: Obtain access tokens - Server API - Documentation - Lark Developer
auth.snippet:
To improve API security, Lark uses an access token mechanism. When calling APIs, the access token authenticates the caller's identity and permissions. This informs Lark who is accessing app data and resources.
The access token is the key to accessing the Lark Open Platform, binding the caller identity, as well as all data access and API call permissions obtained by the app together, allowing the app to perform read and write operations on resources. It is recommended that developers have a thorough understanding of Lark's access token mechanism before starting formal development.
## Introduction to access tokens
The Lark Open Platform provides different types of access tokens for authenticating the calling party's identity. In the actual development process, you can choose the appropriate access token based on your business needs.
| Access Token Type | Requires User Authorization | Description |
|---|---|---|
| tenant_access_token | No | The credentials required to call the API as an app. The range of readable and writable data is determined by the app's own [data permission range](/document/home/introduction-to-scope-and-authorization/configure-app-data-permissions). The value of this type of credential is prefixed with `t-`, and the example value is: `t-24b5bf4e00b2af1234`. |
| user_access_token | is | The credentials required when calling the API as a user. The range of readable and writable data is determined by the user's data permission range. The value of this type of credential is prefixed with `u-`, and the example value is: `u-Lr1RT7S8fS03mT1234`. |
| app_access_token | No | The short-term token for app identity, the open platform identifies the caller's app identity based on the app_access_token. The value of this type of credential is prefixed with `a-` or `t-`, and the example value is: `a-24b5cef00b1234`. |
## How to choose different types of access tokens
APIs may support one or multiple types of access tokens. Different access tokens represent different resource access permissions. Therefore, different access tokens may provide different data information.
1. Confirm the supported access tokens for the API.
When calling the API, the access token needs to be filled in the HTTP request header. In the request header section of the Lark Open Platform API documentation, you can check the supported access token types for that API.
2. Choose the appropriate access token.

auth.title: Obtain user_access_token - Documentation - Lark Developer
auth.snippet:
Obtains the logged-in user's ID that corresponds to the login pre-authorization code.
## Request
| Facts | |
|---|---|
| HTTP URL | https://open.larksuite.com/open-apis/authen/v1/access_token |
| HTTP Method | POST |
| Supported app types | Custom apps Store apps |
| Required scopes | None |
| Required field scopes | The response body of the API contains the following sensitive fields, and they will be returned only after corresponding scopes are added. If you do not need the fields, it is not recommended that you request the scopes. Obtain user's email information Only custom apps Obtain user ID Only custom apps Obtain user's mobile number Only custom apps Obtain user's employment information |
### Request header
| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Authorization | string | Yes | app_access_token **Value format**: "Bearer `access_token`" **Example value**: "Bearer a-7f1bcd13fc57d46bac21793a18e560" [Learn more about obtaining and using access_token.](https://open.larksuite.com/document/ukTMukTMukTM/uMTNz4yM1MjLzUzM) |
| Content-Type | string | Yes | **Fixed value**: "application/json; charset=utf-8" |
### Request body
| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| grant_type | string | Yes | The auth type, whose value is "authorization_code" in this process **Example value**: "authorization_code" |
| code | string | Yes | From the [Request authentication](https://open.larksuite.com/document/ukTMukTMukTM/ukzN4UjL5cDO14SO3gTN) process. The user is automatically redirected to the redirect_uri with this parameter via a 302 redirect after login by scanning the QR code. **Example value**: "xMSldislSkdK" |
### Request body example
```
{    "grant_type": "authorization_code",    "code": "xMSldislSkdK"}
```

auth.title: Calling APIs - Server API - Documentation - Lark Developer
auth.snippet:
To facilitate developers in calling the API conveniently, Lark Open Platform provides Java SDK, Golang SDK, and NodeJS SDK. For detailed information about the SDKs, see [Server SDK](https://open.larksuite.com/document/ukTMukTMukTM/uETO1YjLxkTN24SM5UjN). This article introduces the basic API calling methods.
## Prerequisites
- Before calling the server APIs, you need to complete the steps of creating an app, [applying for permissions](https://open.larksuite.com/document/ukTMukTMukTM/uQjN3QjL0YzN04CN2cDN), [obtaining an access token](https://open.larksuite.com/document/ukTMukTMukTM/uMTNz4yM1MjLzUzM), and [setting IP allowlist](https://open.larksuite.com/document/ukTMukTMukTM/ucTMxYjL3ETM24yNxEjN).
- When calling the server API, you need to include the access token in the request header `Authorization: Bearer <access token>`.
- When calling the server API, you need to use the HTTPS protocol and UTF-8 encoding.

You can use the [Send message](https://open.larksuite.com/document/uAjLw4CM/ukTMukTMukTM/reference/im-v1/message/create) interface to send messages to employees within an organization. Based on the interface documentation, prior to calling this interface, you need to obtain the `tenant_access_token`.
1. Refer to [Obtaining an access token](https://open.larksuite.com/document/ukTMukTMukTM/uMTNz4yM1MjLzUzM) to obtain the `tenant_access_token`.
The example request for obtaining the token is as follows. Please replace `app_id` and `app_secret` with the actual values.
```
curl -X POST 'https://open.larksuite.com/open-apis/auth/v3/tenant_access_token/internal/'-H 'Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8'-d '{  "app_id": "<app_id>",  "app_secret": "<app_secret>"}'
```
2. Based on the request parameter description in the documentation, call the [Send message](https://open.larksuite.com/document/uAjLw4CM/ukTMukTMukTM/reference/im-v1/message/create) interface.

Choose the appropriate access token based on the scope of user information you need.

auth.title: Get authorization code - Server API - Documentation - Lark Developer
auth.snippet:
This API is used to initiate user authorization. After the user consents to the authorization, the application will receive an authorization code, referred to as `code`. Please note that the authorization code is valid for 5 minutes and can only be used once.
## Notes
- This interface is actually an authorization page, suitable for the authorization scenario of web applications. When user authorization is required, the application should redirect the user to this authorization page. After the user clicks authorize on the authorization page (when the web application is opened in the Lark client, it can directly jump without confirmation), the browser will redirect to the address specified by `redirect_uri` and carry the `code` query parameter (i.e., authorization code).
- Developers can use the authorization code to obtain a `user_access_token` to call the OpenAPI (e.g. [Get User Information](https://open.larksuite.com/document/uAjLw4CM/ukTMukTMukTM/reference/authen-v1/user_info/get)). For detailed steps on obtaining a `user_access_token`, refer to [Get user_access_token](https://open.larksuite.com/document/uAjLw4CM/ukTMukTMukTM/authentication-management/access-token/get-user-access-token).
- By using this endpoint along with [Get user_access_token](https://open.larksuite.com/document/uAjLw4CM/ukTMukTMukTM/authentication-management/access-token/get-user-access-token) and [Get user information](https://open.larksuite.com/document/uAjLw4CM/ukTMukTMukTM/reference/authen-v1/user_info/get), the application can implement Lark OAuth login.
- For a complete implementation of the user authorization workflow, refer to the [Web App End User Athorization Guide](https://open.larksuite.com/document/common-capabilities/sso/web-application-end-user-consent/guide).
- Note that when opening the authorization page, you need to declare the user authorization scopes required by the application by appending the `scope` query parameter. For example, the scope key for obtaining basic contact information is `contact:contact.base:readonly`.
- The permissions granted by the user to the application accumulate over time, and the most recently generated `user_access_token` will include all the permissions the user has granted in the past.
- When using the `user_access_token` to call a specific OpenAPI, ensure that this `user_access_token` possesses the [required permissions for the target OpenAPI](https://open.larksuite.com/document/ukTMukTMukTM/uQjN3QjL0YzN04CN2cDN); otherwise, the cal

access.title: open.larksuite.com/llms.txt
access.snippet:
**App authentication**
- **API permissions (scopes)**: In the process of developing an application, you may need to call server-side APIs or listen to subscribed events. Such operations may involve accessing the privacy information of the enterprise or users, or may need to operate on the application data of the enterprise or users. For security reasons, you need to apply for corresponding permissions for the application, and only after the enterprise administrator approves can the application proceed with subsequent API calls or event listening. [Apply for API permissions](https://open.larksuite.com/document/server-docs/getting-started/overview-of-app-scopes)
- **Access tokens (access_token)**
- tenant_access_token: The credentials required to call the API as an app. The range of readable and writable data is determined by the app's own data permission range. This access credential is suitable for automated operations that do not require user login, such as when the application bot calls the Send Message API to push message notifications to a specified conversation. [Get tenant_access_token for custom app](https://open.larksuite.com/document/server-docs/getting-started/api-access-token/auth-v3/tenant_access_token_internal)
- user_access_token: The credentials required when calling the API as a user. The range of readable and writable data is determined by the user's data permission range. This access credential is applicable for operations performed on behalf of the user after authorization login, such as calling the Create Bitable API with the user_access_token. The owner of the created Bitable will be the user corresponding to the user_access_token. Obtaining user_access_token follows standard OAuth 2.0. [Learn more](https://open.larksuite.com/document/common-capabilities/sso/web-application-end-user-consent/guide)

access.title: Lark Integration
access.snippet:
To connect this integration, we require the following:
- A Lark organization account.
- Access to the Lark Developer Console, to create a custom (self-built) app.
- A Lark administrator of your organization, to approve the app.
- Any Lark plan, including Starter. Custom apps can call the Lark API on every plan.
### **Scopes**
- **contact:department.organize:readonly** - for retrieving your organization's departments.
- **contact:user.base:readonly** - for retrieving the members of each department and their names.
- **contact:user.employee:readonly** - for retrieving each user's status and role.
- **contact:user.email:readonly** - for retrieving user email addresses.
- **tenant:tenant:readonly** - for retrieving your Lark organization's name and ID.
- **contact:contact** - required only for performing actions within Torii (Create User, Update User and Delete User).
- **contact:user.id:readonly** - required only for the Update User and Delete User actions, to find the user by email.

1. Sign in to the [Lark Developer Console](https://open.larksuite.com/app) as a member of your Lark organization.
2. Create a custom (self-built) app for your organization. Enter an app name, a description and an icon, and save.
**Step 2: Enable the API permissions**
1. In the app's page in the Developer Console, open the permissions management page (under the development configuration section).
2. On the API permissions tab, select the scopes listed in the Scopes section above and enable them.
3. Set the app's contact permission scope to **All members**, so that Torii can see every user and department in your organization.

access.title: Apply for API permission - Server API - Documentation - Lark Developer
access.snippet:
During app development, you may need to call server APIs of the open platform services, or listen to subscribed events, etc. These operations may require access to tenant and user privacy information or involve manipulation of tenant and user app data. For security reasons, you need to apply for the corresponding permissions for your app. The permissions will take effect only after the app review is approved, and subsequently the app can invoke [server APIs](https://open.larksuite.com/document/ukTMukTMukTM/uYTM5UjL2ETO14iNxkTN/server-api-list) or listen to subscribed [event list](https://open.larksuite.com/document/ukTMukTMukTM/uYDNxYjL2QTM24iN0EjN/event-list). In simple terms, the API permissions (Scope) of an app determine which server-side capabilities the app can use.

Taking the [Get user information](https://open.larksuite.com/document/uAjLw4CM/ukTMukTMukTM/reference/contact-v3/user/get) interface as an example, in the corresponding API document, you can obtain information about the permission requirements and field permission requirements of the interface.

1. Log in to the [Developer Consle](https://open.larksuite.com/app), and enter the designated self-built application.
2. Enter **Development Configuration** > **Permissions & Scopes** function page in the left navigation bar.
3. On the **API Scopes** tab, select the permission required to call the API.
4.

1. Go to the specified store app in the [Developer Console](https://open.larksuite.com/app).
2. Go to **Development Configuration** > **Permissions & Scopes** in the left navigation pane.
3. Apply for permissions in the **Manage scopes** area.
4. After the selection is complete, click **Add in bulk** in the upper right corner of the **Manage scopes** area.
5. In the **Reminder** dialog box, after confirming that the requested permission list is correct, click **Confirm**.

mcp.title: raw.githubusercontent.com/larksuite/lark-openapi-mcp/main/README.md
mcp.snippet:
This is the Feishu/Lark official OpenAPI MCP (Model Context Protocol) tool designed to help users quickly connect to the Feishu/Lark platform and enable efficient collaboration between AI Agents and Feishu/Lark. The tool encapsulates Feishu/Lark Open Platform API interfaces as MCP tools, allowing AI assistants to directly call these interfaces and implement various automation scenarios such as document processing, conversation management, calendar scheduling, and more.
## Preparation
### Creating a Feishu/Lark Application
Before using the lark-mcp tool, you need to create a Feishu/Lark application:
1. Visit the [Feishu Open Platform](https://open.feishu.cn/) or [Lark Open Platform](https://open.larksuite.com/) and log in
2. Click "Console" and create a new application
3. Obtain the App ID and App Secret, which will be used for API authentication
4. Add the necessary permissions for your application based on your usage scenario
5. If you need to call APIs as a user, set the OAuth 2.0 redirect URL to http://localhost:3000/callback

Based on your usage scenario, lark-mcp supports configuring different domain environments:
**Feishu (China Version)**:
- Default uses `https://open.feishu.cn` domain
- Suitable for users in China
**Lark (International Version)**:
- Uses `https://open.larksuite.com` domain
- Suitable for overseas users or international version of Lark
To switch to the international version of Lark, add the `--domain` parameter in your configuration:
```json
{
"mcpServers": {
"lark-mcp": {
"command": "npx",
"args": [
"-y",
"@larksuiteoapi/lark-mcp",
"mcp",
"-a",
"<your_app_id>",
"-s",
"<your_app_secret>",
"--domain",
"https://open.larksuite.com"
]
}
}
}
```

mcp.title: Advanced configuration - Lark CLI - Documentation - Lark Developer
mcp.snippet:
The MCP tool supports a wide range of command parameters, allowing flexible configuration for suitable MCP startup commands. Detailed usage instructions for each parameter are provided below in **Parameter usage examples**.

1. Run the following command in your local terminal to install lark-mcp.
```
npm install @larksuiteoapi/lark-mcp -g
```

After installing lark-mcp locally, you can use the MCP tool persistently (supported command parameters are referred to in the **Command Parameters** section below). Taking [Trae](https://www.trae.com.cn/) as an example, the global installation steps are explained as follows:
- Global installation: installs to a global path (/usr/local/lib), commands are persistent, and system-level commands are available. Suitable for scenarios where command line tools are used frequently.
- NPX installation: described in the [Install and use OpenAPI MCP](https://open.larksuite.com/document/uAjLw4CM/ukTMukTMukTM/mcp_integration/mcp_installation) document. This method allows quick installation and use, but the command is not persistent as it is installed in the system's temporary cache, deleted after execution. Suitable for quick trials or one-time usage.

2. Open the Cursor tool.
3. Open the terminal within the tool.
4. Execute the following command to log in to OpenAPI MCP as a user:
```
lark-mcp login -a <your_app_id> -s <your_app_secret>
```

### lark-mcp mcp
The supported command parameters of `lark-mcp mcp` are described in the table below.
| Parameter | Abbreviation | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--app-id` | `-a` | App ID of the Lark application. | `-a cli_xxxx` |
| `--app-secret` | `-s` | App Secret of the Lark application. | `-s xxxx` |
| `--domain` | `-d` | API domain of the Lark Open Platform, default is the Lark domain. | `-d https://open.larksuite.com` |
| `--tools` | `-t` | List of MCP tools that need to be enabled. Refer to [tools](https://github.com/larksuite/lark-openapi-mcp/tree/main/docs) and pass the corresponding **MCP tool names**. - Support passing in preset toolsets. For example, if you pass in the preset toolset for messages and groups (preset.im.default), the specified range of message and group APIs will be enabled. For details on usage, see the below **Preset tool sets** section.

| `--mode` | `-m` | Transmission mode. Optional values are: - stdio (default) - sse - streamable | `-m sse` |
| `--oauth` | None | Configurable parameter for SSE/Streamable transmission mode, enabling automatic use

mcp.title: GitHub - junyuan-qi/lark-mcp-server
mcp.snippet:
# Lark MCP Server
A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server implementation for Lark/Feishu, enabling MCP-compatible applications to interact with Lark's various collaboration capabilities.
## Overview
Lark MCP Server provides a bridge between AI models and Lark's collaboration platform by implementing the Model Context Protocol (MCP) specification. This server allows AI assistants to:
- Send messages to Lark users
- Retrieve calendar events
- Create new calendar events
- Add attendees to calendar events
The server uses the standard I/O (stdio) transport layer to communicate with MCP clients, making it compatible with various AI model implementations that support the MCP standard.
## Features
- **Message Sending**: AI models can send direct messages to Lark users
- **Calendar Management**:
- List events within a specific time range
- Create new calendar events with customizable details
- Add various types of attendees to events (users, groups, meeting rooms, external emails)

1. Clone the repository:
```
git clone https://github.com/junyuan-qi/lark-mcp-server.git
cd lark-mcp-server
```

### Connecting with an MCP Client
The server communicates via standard input/output (stdio). MCP clients can connect to the server by launching it as a child process and communicating through its stdin/stdout channels.

#### 2. Add the Lark MCP server configuration
Add the following configuration to the `mcpServers` section of your `claude_desktop_config.json`:
```
{
"mcpServers": {
"lark-mcp-server": {
"command": "node",
"args": ["/path/to/lark-mcp-server/build/index.js"],
"env": {
"LARK_APP_ID": "your_app_id",
"LARK_APP_SECRET": "your_app_secret",
"LARK_USER_ID": "target_user_id",
"LARK_CALENDAR_ID": "target_calendar_id",
"LARK_USER_ACCESS_TOKEN": "your_user_access_token"
}
}
}
}
```
Replace the path and environment variables with your actual values. This configuration tells Claude Desktop how to launch the Lark MCP server and what environment variables to provide.
#### 3. Restart Claude Desktop
For the changes to take effect:
1. Completely quit Claude Desktop (not just close the window)
2. Start Claude Desktop again
3. Look for an icon in the UI to verify the Lark MCP server is connected
Once connected, Claude will be able to send messages to Lark users and manage calendar events on your behalf.

For more information about the Model Context Protocol, visit the [MCP Documentation](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/introduction).

mcp.snippet:
# Lark MCP Server
Custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for Lark/Feishu - read access to Base (Bitable), Docs, Wiki, and Sheets.
## Features
- **Base (Bitable)** - Read databases, tables, records, and views
- **Docs** - Read document content and blocks
- **Wiki** - Navigate knowledge base spaces and pages
- **Sheets** - Read spreadsheet data
## Quick Start
### 1. Install
```
cd lark-mcp-server
npm install
npm run build
```
### 2. Configure
Create a `.env` file:
```
LARK_APP_ID=your_app_id
LARK_APP_SECRET=your_app_secret
```
### 3. Run
```
# Stdio mode (for Claude Desktop)
node dist/index.js
# HTTP mode (for remote access)
node dist/index.js --http
# Server runs on http://localhost:3100
```
### 4. Connect to Claude Desktop
Add to `claude_desktop_config.json`:
```
{
"mcpServers": {
"lark-mcp": {
"command": "node",
"args": ["/absolute/path/to/lark-mcp-server/build/index.js"],
"env": {
"LARK_APP_ID": "your_app_id",
"LARK_APP_SECRET": "your_app_secret"
}
}
}
}
```
## Available Tools
### Base/Bitable (8 tools)
- `bitable_get_app` - Get Base app info
- `bitable_list_tables` - List tables
- `bitable_list_records` - List records
- `bitable_get_record` - Get single record
- `bitable_batch_get_records` - Batch get records
- `bitable_search_records` - Search records
- `bitable_list_views` - List views
- `bitable_get_view` - Get view
### Documents (4 tools)
- `docs_list_documents` - List documents
- `docs_get_content` - Get text content
- `docs_get_raw_content` - Get raw JSON
- `docs_get_blocks` - Get block structure
### Wiki (3 tools)
- `wiki_get_node` - Get page info
- `wiki_list_spaces` - List wiki spaces
- `wiki_list_nodes` - List pages
### Sheets (4 tools)
- `sheet_get` - Get spreadsheet info
- `sheet_list_sheets` - List sheets
- `sheet_get_values` - Read cells
- `sheet_get_values_batch` - Read multiple ranges
### Drive (1 tool)
- `drive_list_files` - List Drive files

mcp.snippet:
Lark Open Platform provides a remote MCP Server configuration feature that supports the Streamable HTTP transmission protocol, allowing users to securely and efficiently integrate and use rich Lark open capabilities in cloud scenarios with AI agents such as Cursor, Trae, Claude, and n8n via one-click integration.
## Configuring the MCP Server
Create a remote MCP service on the Lark MCP Configuration Platform and customize tools (i.e., Lark Open Platform server-side APIs) to flexibly build the MCP tools your business needs.
All tools are called via API under the identity of the currently logged-in user (user_access_token). Details:
- During the configuration process, the system guides you to complete the authorization operation for the logged-in user with one click. The MCP Server can only call tools on behalf of the user after authorization.
- The user_access_token itself has an expiry time. The remote MCP Server configuration feature supports automatic refreshing of the token before expiration.

Take Cursor as an example, to use Lark MCP services inside the AI agent.
1. Open a new chat session on the right side of the tool.
- Select **Agent** at the bottom left.
- Choose the large model as **Auto** or manually select any model (different models may have different outcomes).
2. Fill in your specific business requirements in the input box.
